a1
A famine came. The Lord told Isaac: do not go to Egypt. Stay in this land, and I will bless you.
b1
Isaac sowed crops in Gerar, and that year he harvested a hundred times what he planted. He became very rich.
b2
The Philistines grew jealous. They filled in the wells Abraham's servants had dug. Abimelech said: leave us, you have become too powerful.
c1
Isaac moved away and dug Abraham's wells again, and gave them his father's names.
c2
Herdsmen quarreled over two wells. Isaac named them Quarrel and Opposition.
c3
He dug a third, and no one fought over it. He named it Rehoboth: now the Lord has made room for us.
d1
At Beersheba the Lord said: do not be afraid, I am with you.
d2
Then Abimelech came and said: we see that the Lord is with you. They made peace, and shared a feast.
h1
When others quarreled over the wells, Isaac did not fight. He moved on, and dug again.
h2
In time, the Lord made room for him.
h3
Not every quarrel is worth winning. Some are worth walking away from.
h4
Today, choose peace, and trust God to make room.
i
Where can you choose peace instead of winning?
